newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus Hellenic may bid for Greek bank.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus Hellenic may bid for Greek bank.

text.p: Cyprus-based Hellenic Bank has expressed an interest in taking a stake in Greek state-controlled Bank of Central Greece, a senior official of Hellenic said on Wednesday.
"There is an interest. We are examining it in the framework of exploring all available options of expanding into Greece," Yiannis Telonis, head of marketing services told Reuters.
The two dominant banks in Cyprus -- Bank of Cyprus and the Cyprus Popular Bank -- have dismissed reports in the Greek press that they too are interested in bidding for a stake in the Greek bank.
Hellenic, the island's third largest bank, is eyeing Greece for future expansion and has already applied to the Central Bank of Greece for a commercial licence.
"We have not got the actual licence yet but we have all the indications that there are no problems. It is just a matter of formalities now," said Telonis.

"We are setting this interest within the context of exploring all options towards expanding to Greece. It is not the only option we have. It is one of the options and we are exploring all options," he said.
Cypriot-owned Hellenic, created in 1976, bought the Cyprus onshore operations of Barclays Bank a year ago in a deal worth 8.5 million pounds ($16.5 million).

It reported preliminary pre-tax profits of 3.4 million pounds in 1996, compared with 4.75 million in 1995. Operating profit last year was up 38.7 percent, but the cost of the Barclays purchase and an early-retirement scheme after the merger were included in the 1996 results.
The bank has 120 branches and employs 1,150 people. ($= 0.516 pounds) -- Nicosia newsroom 357 2 365089
